question.prompt: A bee starts flying from point \(P_0.\) She flies \(1\) inch due east to point \(P_1.\) For \(j \ge 1,\) once the bee reaches point \(P_j,\) she turns \(30^\circ\) counterclockwise and then flies \(j + 1\) inches straight to point \(P_{j+1}.\) When the bee reaches \(P_{2015}\) she is exactly \(a\sqrt b + c\sqrt d\) inches away from \(P_0,\) where \(a,\) \(b,\) \(c,\) and \(d\) are positive integers and \(b\) and \(d\) are not divisible by the square of any prime. What is \(a + b + c + d?\)

solutions.explanation:
Flight \(n\), from \(P_{n-1}\) to \(P_n\), has length \(n\) and direction \(30(n-1)^\circ\) counterclockwise from east. Directions repeat every \(12\) flights. Because \(2016=168\cdot12\), temporarily add flight \(2016\), sum complete blocks, and then subtract that last flight.

Take east and north as the positive coordinate directions. For \(t=0,1,\ldots,5\), let \(u_t\) be the displacement of a one-inch flight in direction \(30t^\circ\). Within a block, pair flight \(12k+r\) with flight \(12k+r+6\), where \(1\le r\le6\). Their directions are opposite and their lengths differ by \(6\), so their combined displacement is
\[
(12k+r)u_{r-1}-(12k+r+6)u_{r-1}
=-6u_{r-1}.
\]
Thus every twelve-flight block has the same displacement,
\[
-6(u_0+u_1+\cdots+u_5).
\]
To add these six direction vectors, pair the directions \(30^\circ\) and \(150^\circ\): their horizontal components cancel, while their vertical components add to \(1\). Likewise, the directions \(60^\circ\) and \(120^\circ\) contribute \((0,\sqrt3)\). The remaining east and north vectors contribute \((1,1)\). Hence
\[
u_0+u_1+\cdots+u_5=(1,2+\sqrt3).
\]
After \(168\) blocks, the displacement from \(P_0\) to \(P_{2016}\) is therefore
\[
-1008(1,2+\sqrt3).
\]
Flight \(2016\) points in direction \(330^\circ\), since its direction index \(2015\) leaves remainder \(11\) on division by \(12\). Its displacement is
\[
2016(\cos330^\circ,\sin330^\circ)
=1008(\sqrt3,-1).
\]
Subtracting this flight gives the displacement to \(P_{2015}\):
\[
-1008(1,2+\sqrt3)-1008(\sqrt3,-1)
=-1008(1+\sqrt3,1+\sqrt3).
\]
Its two components have equal absolute value, so the distance is
\[
1008(1+\sqrt3)\sqrt2
=1008\sqrt2+1008\sqrt6.
\]
Since \(2\) and \(6\) are squarefree, the requested sum is
\[
1008+2+1008+6=\boxed{2024},
\]
choice \(\mathrm{B}\).
solutions.title: Pair opposite flights in twelve-flight blocks
Sum displacements using a twelfth root of unity
